releases.title: Answer by link
changes: Heard from someone another way, in a chat or on a call? New item in the inbox files it: who asked, their email if you have it, and your reply, in one go.

Any item can have a link of its own. It opens the item, who asked and its public comments with no sign-in, whether or not your feedback page is on, and never shows contact details, pages, browsers, answers or files.
Whoever has the link can comment, and their comments wait for your approval. Turn the link off and it stops at once, or make a new one and the old one stops.
With an API key, an agent can file a question, answer it and get its link in one call.
Comments waiting for approval stack like the others again, instead of lying in one row.

releases.title: Follow what you sent
changes: Leave your email and the form offers to confirm it with a 6-digit code, right after you send. Skip it and nothing changes.
Signed in with a confirmed email, Your feedback shows everything you sent, on every project, with where it stands.
Teams can reply to a confirmed sender: the reply joins the item's thread and arrives by email, with a link to stop emails. The sender writes back from Your feedback, and the inbox shows they replied.
Feedback never emails an address nobody confirmed. Private notes stay with the team.

releases.title: Accounts for agents
changes: An agent building a site for someone with no feedback account can make one for it: one project and a key that reaches only that project. Holm makes it solve a short puzzle first and allows ten a minute.
Until someone keeps it, the project's form takes no files and up to 100 items a day, and it is deleted after 90 days unused.
Its inbox link offers to keep it in your account. Signed in, it is one click, and only the first person to keep it can.
Any API key can replace itself with a new one.

releases.title: Inbox links
changes: An owner, or an agent with an API key, can ask for a link that opens a project's inbox without signing in. Each link opens once, within five minutes.

The inbox it opens locks after five minutes without activity. A bar along the top empties while nobody is there and fills again at any touch; the clock beside it says how long is left, and Lock ends it at once.
Once locked, the page says so and keeps nothing of the inbox, even on Back. Open it again with a new link.

releases.title: Opens at once
changes: The form now loads in the background once the page is idle, so it opens the moment someone clicks.
It still reports the page someone is on when they open it, even on sites that change pages without reloading.
Readers who asked their browser to save data, and sites that set data-preload="hover", load it on hover as before.

releases.title: Videos play in place
changes: A video someone sends plays right on the item, under its message, with its name, size and download link beneath it.
If your browser can’t play it (phone videos often use a format some browsers lack), the item says so beside the download link instead of showing a broken player.

releases.title: Your own computer isn't a site
changes: Where it's live lists pages on localhost or a private network, like a developer's copy, on a line of their own, with no Allow button.
They no longer count as a project's website, and can't crowd real sites out of the list.

releases.title: Room for hundreds
changes: Your projects sit in a panel that scrolls on its own: the page doesn't move, and the footer stays at the bottom.
Each project shows the site it's on, and its feedback page, at a glance.
Every project gets an icon. Pick another in Design, from 48, or its first letter; a logo still wins. It shows on the form and your page too.

An inbox built for hundreds: sort by newest, oldest, votes, rating or last change; filter by when, where it came from, whether you can reply and whether it's on your page; search every word, or #12. Fifty at a time, with a count and a Clear.
On a phone, the filters fold behind one button and the statuses scroll in a row.
Press / to search the inbox.
Feedback about this app now has a home: Feedback, in the footer.

releases.title: A button people want on their site
changes: The form on your site wears your cover, logo, title and words, in light, dark or your visitors' own theme.
The button eases in, lifts on hover and turns into a close cross; the panel springs open and grows with what's in it. On a phone it's a sheet from the bottom.
An optional star rating, with faces that cheer up as the stars go up. The inbox filters by it and Stats show the average.
A Design tab for the look, with a preview that runs the real button on a stand-in page, at a computer's width or a phone's.
Set up shows where the button is live, with sites to allow in a tap. The snippet is one short line, and changes need no new one.
Dropdowns, switches and segmented controls drawn to match the app, and a copy button joined to every snippet.
"Bug" is now "Issue", which suits more kinds of trouble.
This changelog.

releases.title: A form of your own
changes: Ask for an email or a phone number, optional or required.
Add up to eight questions: a short answer, a dropdown, one choice or checkboxes.
Filter the inbox by kind, by any answer, by photos or by words.
Each item is a thread for your team: notes and every change, in order.

releases.title: For places and events
changes: A project can be for a restaurant, a shop or an event: Praise, Problem and Idea.
On a phone, one tap opens the camera, and a photo alone is enough to send.
Your feedback page gets a title, description, logo and cover.
Stats count QR scans and email visits on their own; Share can email the link.

releases.title: Link previews of its own
changes: A shared link shows feedback's title, words and picture.

releases.title: Quicker tabs
changes: The button carries the app's smiling-bubble mark.
Switching a project's tabs changes only what's below them.

releases.title: A page of its own
changes: A feedback page at your own address, with votes and comments you approve.
Files on feedback: pictures, videos, PDFs and text.
A QR code and a poster to print.
Stats per project and for your account; light, dark or system theme.

releases.title: A face for the app
changes: A smiling speech bubble for the icon, the favicon and the sign-in page.

releases.title: Keys for agents
changes: API keys, so a script or a coding agent can set up a project and sort its inbox.

releases.title: A feedback button for any website
changes: One script tag adds a button and a small form to any site.
An inbox per project, tinted by status, with private notes.
A public board of the items you choose, with votes.
